Grade every segment of a species' groups by its tuned curve

Source: R/grade_species.R
knw_grade_species.Rd

Reads the species' segments (knw_link_segments()), walks every accessible segment with a gradient (on any edge type and at any gradient: wetland lines, river polygons and steep segments included, and whatever its size) from its downstream end to the first river of the pick's exc_q, or of the curve's q when the pick has no exception, and grades them all (knw_grade()). The curve reads size and distance jointly, so every graded segment needs its own distance, whether or not it passes the size test. For the pick the curve was fitted on, the two rivers are the same.

Usage

knw_grade_species(
  connector,
  schema,
  species,
  wsg,
  curve,
  pick,
  stage = "rear",
  workers = 4L,
  src = "pick",
  ref_edge = NULL,
  cache = "knw.walk_cache"
)

Arguments

connector

a function returning a DBI connection (each walk worker opens its own).

schema

character(1) link persist schema.

species

character(1) species code.

wsg

character the species' groups.

curve

knw_tune_curve()'s result for the species and stage. It must have been fitted on link's segment gradient (curve$cols[["grad"]] is segment_gradient), the gradient the segments are graded on (#92).

pick

the recommended rule row.

stage

"rear" or "spawn".

workers

integer(1) walk workers.

src

character(1) the flow source.

ref_edge

integer or NULL (the default): the stream-branch edge types the reference rate is taken over. NULL takes the curve's own edge_stream, the edge types of the visits it was fitted on (#72), and a curve that carries none takes knw_tune_run()'s default edge_stream.

cache

the walk cache knw_link_walks() reads and keeps walks in ("knw.walk_cache"), or FALSE to walk every start.

Value

A list: grades, one row per segment with the segment's keys, length_metre, access, accessible, the stage's flag, size, dist_m, dist_status, target_in_group (TRUE where the river the walk found lies in the segment's own watershed group, FALSE where it lies in another, which link's walk, one group's table at a time, cannot see; NA where no river was found), rate, grade, grade_class; reference; ref_edge, the edge types the reference was taken over; q, the river size walked to; walk, the walk's convention ("bank": the distance ends at the river's bank, #73); walk_md5, the walk's code (knw_walk_md5(), #87); counts (segments, accessible, walked starts, starts read from the walk cache and walked, segments whose walk was found, none or other, graded, no size, no gradient); walk_minutes.

Details

dist_m also serves knw_compare_rules() as the exception's distance. That is why a segment with no size is walked although it is not graded (the exception admits a segment whose size fails, missing included), and why a pick's own exc_q wins: a candidate whose river differs from the curve's gets a correct exception and a grade that is not comparable.

The curve was fitted on stream-branch visits outside lakes, wetlands and river polygons, so a grade off that branch is an extrapolation: a river-polygon segment often reads the curve near 0 m (about half of their km within 1 m for grayling, four fifths for chinook) and at sizes few visits had, and a wetland or lake segment lies outside the visits it was fitted on. The reference rate that reads 1 is therefore taken over the stream branch alone (ref_edge; Al, 2026-10-19): over every accessible segment, river-polygon segments make up most of the top 5 % for chinook, coho, steelhead and cutthroat, whose reference rises 1.4 to 4 times (chinook's from 0.14 to 0.52); for bull trout, grayling and rainbow the two references are within 7 %.

A walk that finds no river of q (none: the sea first; no_parent; too_many_hops) leaves dist_m missing, which the grade reads as the distance cap, as knw_tune_curve() censors such visits. dist_status says which, and is no_walk for a segment outside the walk set (not accessible, or with no gradient).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
pg <- function() DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), bigint = "numeric")
g <- knw_grade_species(pg, "fresh_default", "CH", c("BULK", "MORR"),
                       out$CH_rear$curve, out$CH_rear$pick)
} # }
